title: Albania's security agency chief warns of continuing Iranian cyberattacks
date_note: The page gives only its publication day (25 November 2026); the interview date is not stated.
actor: Iran (as stated by the Albanian agency director)
summary: In an interview with ANN News, relayed by ABEMA TIMES, Bledar Kaçia, director of Albania's State Security Agency, said Iranian cyberattacks on Albania have continued into 2026. He said the attackers now run smaller, more frequent operations that steal and leak data and apply psychological pressure through Telegram. He urged joint attribution, common sanctions and rapid information sharing.
plain: Albania's security agency chief says Iran-linked cyberattacks on the country have continued into 2026, now as smaller, more frequent data theft and leak operations, and asks other countries to cooperate.
exec: An Albanian official says Iranian attacks continue as smaller, more frequent data-theft and leak operations, and calls for joint attribution and sanctions.

validation.note: Only the ABEMA TIMES report (citing an ANN News interview), carried by infoseek, was read; the agency's own statement was not found.
